section_summary: This section comprises State Department despatches, interdepartmental correspondence with the Department of the Army, National Security Council memoranda, and detailed economic reports concerning post-war Japan's economic recovery and demographic trends between February and August 1948. Key topics include debates over population forecasts and tuberculosis eradication, coordination between civilian and military agencies regarding Far Eastern Commission industrial policy paper FEC 242/32, and allocation of congressional GARIOA rehabilitation funds among Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyu Islands. It also features extensive documentation on Japanese business conditions, including business leaders' reluctance to invest due to deconcentration and purge policies, Commonwealth reactions to proposed Japanese industrial levels, and comprehensive GHQ and Economic Stabilization Board reviews of production, prices, and trade.

subfiles.about: Despatch forwarding demographic studies of Japan's future population and discussing the lack of population control measures.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards a GHQ memorandum criticizing Economic Stabilization Board population forecasts as too low and notes the lack of Japanese population control efforts.
subfiles.title: Demographic Studies of Japan's Future Population

subfiles.about: Memorandum analyzing and criticizing the Economic Stabilization Board's population increase assumptions.
subfiles.from: M. Stone, Population Branch, Research and Programs Division, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: A GHQ analysis argues that the Economic Stabilization Board underestimated future population by projecting an unrealistic decline in birth rates and failing to reflect recent demographic trends.
subfiles.title: Criticism of ESB Population Increase Assumptions

subfiles.about: Newspaper clipping reporting on a planned Japanese government bill to mandate BCG inoculations against tuberculosis.
subfiles.summary: Article reporting on a planned Japanese Welfare Ministry bill to introduce compulsory BCG vaccinations to combat tuberculosis.
subfiles.title: Drive is Decided to Wipe Out TB

subfiles.about: Letter recommending that the U.S. representative on the Far Eastern Commission oppose approval of FEC 242/32 prior to National Security Council policy decisions.
subfiles.summary: Secretary Royall urges Secretary Marshall to instruct General McCoy to delay approval of FEC 242/32 pending National Security Council review.
subfiles.title: Policy Towards Japanese Industry - Level of Economic Life in Japan

subfiles.about: Letter concerning instructions to General McCoy regarding the Far Eastern Commission paper on Japanese industrial levels.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State agrees to delay action on FEC 242/32 and forwards Secretary Royall's letter to General McCoy for information.
subfiles.title: Policy Towards Japanese Industry - Level of Economic Life in Japan (FEC 242/32)

subfiles.about: Memorandum recommending tactical revisions to the draft reply to Secretary Royall concerning FEC 242/32.
subfiles.summary: Allison suggests forwarding Royall's letter to General McCoy to prevent misunderstandings between the State and Army Departments regarding FEC 242/32.
subfiles.title: Attached Letter to Secretary Royall

subfiles.about: Letter transmitting a proposed policy paper on self-support of the Japanese economy for submission to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Wisner transmits a shortened policy paper on Japanese economic self-support based on SANACC 381 for joint submission to SCAP.
subfiles.title: Self-Support of the Japanese Economy

subfiles.about: Letter forwarding copies of correspondence between Secretary Royall and the State Department regarding FEC 242/32 to General McCoy.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman forwards copies of correspondence between Secretary Royall and the State Department regarding FEC 242/32 to General McCoy.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Letters on Policy Towards Japanese Industry (FEC 242/32)

subfiles.about: Letter proposing joint State-Army discussions on the allocation of GARIOA and rehabilitation funds for Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman proposes joint State-Army discussions on allocating GARIOA funds among Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.title: Allocation of Funds for Japan, Korea and the Ryukyus

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a special report on the general economic press, periodicals, and news services of Japan.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwarding a GHQ special report analyzing Japan's principal general economic periodicals, newspapers, and news agencies.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Special Report: General Economic Press of Japan

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a memorandum regarding New Zealand concern over reported U.S. policy on Japan's permitted economic level.
subfiles.summary: Scotten transmits a memorandum on New Zealand concern over reported U.S. proposals permitting a higher economic level for Japan.
subfiles.title: New Zealand Concern over Reported New American Policy on Economic Level for Japan

subfiles.about: Memorandum detailing discussions with New Zealand officials concerning British Commonwealth apprehensions over U.S. economic policy for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Service reports conversations with New Zealand external affairs officials regarding British Commonwealth alarm over a paper indicating the United States might permit a substantially higher economic level for Japan.
subfiles.title: New Zealand Concern over Reported New American Policy on Economic Level for Japan

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation between State and Army officials and National Foreign Trade Council executives regarding economic conditions and American investment in Japan.
subfiles.summary: American business executives discuss obstacles to resuming operations in Japan, citing vague deconcentration laws, the industrial purge, inflation, labor unrest, and excessive military government controls.
subfiles.title: Economic Aspects of the Japanese Occupation

subfiles.about: Memorandum regarding interdepartmental delays in clearing a proposed cable to SCAP concerning the Japanese purge program.
subfiles.summary: Rudlin complains of Department of the Army delays in clearing a proposed State Department cable to SCAP regarding the purge.
subfiles.title: Proposed Cable to SCAP on the Purge Program in Japan

subfiles.about: Memorandum commenting on the proposed apportionment of GARIOA rehabilitation funds among Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.summary: Whitman approves the $75 million Far East rehabilitation allotment but questions the small share for the Ryukyus, lack of integrated Korean planning, and uncoordinated transfers from German GARIOA funds.
subfiles.title: WARX 85777 - Apportionment of Funds for Rehabilitation in Japan, Korea and the Ryukyus

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting and clarifying remarks by New Zealand Minister of Finance Walter Nash regarding economic policy and production levels for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Service forwards and clarifies public statements by New Zealand Finance Minister Walter Nash regarding the necessity of restoring Japanese production and trade to maintain regional peace.
subfiles.title: Views of New Zealand Minister of Finance on Economic Policy for Japan

subfiles.about: Newspaper clipping reporting an address by New Zealand Minister of Finance Walter Nash on world problems and Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Newspaper article reporting Walter Nash's address on world economic recovery, British difficulties, European refugees, and reviving Japanese industrial production.
subfiles.title: Mr. Nash Surveys World Problems

subfiles.about: Memorandum transmitting National Security Resources Board comments on NSC policy recommendations for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bishop forwards to Butterworth comments by Daniel Cox Fahey, Jr. of NSRB on the National Security Council Japan paper.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Comment by Mr. Fahey on NSC Paper on Japan

subfiles.about: Letter proposing implementation measures for NSC 13 to re-establish Japanese trade in Far Eastern markets.
subfiles.summary: Fahey suggests that the State Department, Army, and ECA coordinate to stimulate Japanese export trade by arranging triangular exchanges of Far Eastern commodities for Japanese manufactured goods.
subfiles.title: Implementation of Policy Regarding Japanese Economic Recovery (NSC 13)

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting and reviewing the Japanese Economic Stabilization Board's report on economic conditions for fiscal year 1947.
subfiles.summary: Sebald transmits the Economic Stabilization Board's May 1948 report on Japanese economic conditions alongside Japanese press commentaries. The despatch offers a detailed sector-by-sector critique covering coal, electric power, manufacturing, agriculture, transport, foreign trade, public finance, and labor. Sebald criticizes the Japanese government for complacency and superficial analyses of inflation and rationing failures while avoiding the issue of labor unrest.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of 'Report on Japanese Economic Conditions'

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting copies of the Economic Stabilization Board's rehabilitation plan and GHQ's economic conditions report.
subfiles.summary: Hodge transmits copies of the Economic Stabilization Board's draft rehabilitation plan and GHQ's August 5 report on economic conditions.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Two Basic Reports on Japanese Economy

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting GHQ's report on Japanese economic conditions for June 1948.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwarding GHQ's economic report for June 1948, summarizing trends in industrial production, price movements, and foreign trade bottlenecks.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Report Entitled 'Economic Conditions in Japan'

subfiles.about: Report by the Economic and Scientific Section of GHQ reviewing Japanese industrial production, foreign trade, and price indices for June 1948.
subfiles.from: Research and Programs Division, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: This monthly report by GHQ's Economic and Scientific Section details Japanese economic conditions for June 1948. Industrial production reached a postwar peak of 52.7 percent of prewar levels, bolstered by gains in coal, iron, and machinery, while textiles remained severely depressed. Foreign trade continued to face acute dollar shortages and raw material bottlenecks, and effective consumer prices experienced a temporary sharp increase.
subfiles.title: Economic Conditions in Japan
